data.title: My First React Component

data.title: Interactive Profile Card
data.description: Create a profile card displaying 'Frontend Developer' / 'Learning React JSX Attributes'. Requirements: 1) Declare `const cardClass = "profile-card"` and use it as `className`. 2) A 'Show Message' button that alerts 'Hello React!' on click, initially enabled. 3) A disabled 'Coming Soon' button. 4) Apply CSS class 'profile-heading' to the heading. Do NOT use inline styles.

requirements.text: Must declare and use the 'cardClass' variable as className.
Show Message button must call alert('Hello React!') on click.
Coming Soon button must be disabled.
Heading must use the CSS class 'profile-heading'.

Requirements: 1) Apply CSS class 'card-container' to the wrapping div. 2) Apply CSS class 'profile-heading' to the h1. 3) Apply CSS class 'highlight-text' to the paragraph 'Learning React Styling'. Do NOT use inline styles.

requirements.text: Component name must be ProfileCard.
Must use CSS class 'card-container'.
Must use CSS class 'profile-heading'.
Must use CSS class 'highlight-text'.

data.title: React CSS Modules
data.description: Practice real CSS Modules. In `Button.jsx`, import the styles object from `Button.module.css` and apply a class to the button using `styles.<className>`. Write the actual CSS rules yourself in `Button.module.css` (background color, padding, border-radius, and a hover effect). The button must display the text 'Click Me'. Do NOT use inline styles.

code_test.css: body { margin: 0; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; background-color: #0f172a; font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, sans-serif; }

requirements.text: Component name must be Button.
Must import styles from './Button.module.css'.
Must apply className to the button element.
Button must display the text 'Click Me'.

data.title: React JSX Conditional Statements
data.description:
1. Create a `StatusBadge` component that accepts an `isOnline` boolean prop (default value true).
2. Return a `<div>` element.
3. Use a ternary operator (`? :`) to conditionally set BOTH `className` and text inside the `<div>`.
4. If isOnline is true: className = 'badge-online', text = 'Online'.
5. If isOnline is false: className = 'badge-offline', text = 'Offline'.
6. You must NOT use if/else statements (use ternary only).

requirements.text: Create a React component named StatusBadge.
Accept a boolean prop called isOnline.
Use ternary (? :) to change className based on isOnline.
Use ternary (? :) to display 'Online' or 'Offline'.

data.title: React Component
data.description: Create a function component named `Greeting` that returns an `<h1>` element with the text 'Hello, React!'. Do NOT use any hooks (useState, useEffect, etc.). App must render Greeting inside a div with className='card'.

requirements.text: Component name must be Greeting.
Component must return an h1 element.
The h1 must contain the text 'Hello, React!'.

data.title: Passing Props
data.description: Create a function component named `UserCard` that accepts a `username` prop via the `props` object (do NOT destructure). Return an `<h3>` displaying 'User: {props.username}'. Do NOT use any hooks.

requirements.text: Component name must be UserCard.
Component must accept a prop named username via props object.
Component must return an h3 element.
The h3 must contain 'User: ' followed by the username value.

data.title: Stateful Counter Component
data.description:
Create a `Counter` component using `useState` (initial value 0). Display `count` in an `<h1>`. Add THREE buttons inside a `<div className="btn-group">`:
- `<button className="btn-decrement">Decrement</button>` — decreases count by 1
- `<button className="btn-reset">Reset</button>` — resets count to 0
- `<button className="btn-increment">Increment</button>` — increases count by 1
UI: background #edf2f7, card background #ffffff, counter container class 'counter-container'.

requirements.text: Component name must be Counter.
Must use the useState hook.
Increment button must increase count by 1.
Decrement button must decrease count by 1.
Reset button must set count back to 0.
